subject.title: attach: --print-config prints live MCP token without log-safe mode

question: Should `openclaw attach --print-config` become log-safe by default, with raw bearer-token output available only through an explicit warned opt-in?
rationale: The current output is intentionally usable for manual launch, but it exposes live bearer material; choosing whether and how to preserve raw stdout compatibility is a security-boundary decision rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Safe by default
options.body: Print a redacted summary and a temporary `0600` secret-handoff path, requiring an explicit warned option for raw token output.

options.title: Warning only
options.body: Keep the existing output but add a prominent stderr warning and documentation that stdout contains a live bearer token.

options.title: File handoff only
options.body: Remove raw token printing and require the normal spawned workflow or a protected file-based manual handoff.

recommendation.title: Safe by default
recommendation.body: Print a redacted summary and a temporary `0600` secret-handoff path, requiring an explicit warned option for raw token output.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the launcher, authored its token-config adjustment, and provided the clearest recent attach security-direction review.
